title: The Takeout Lie
editorialNotes: Copy taken from the local brief (rule C4: local wins over Notion). The brief already uses "fond"; no swap needed.
$5,000/year, $3,400/year and $6,700-10,000/year are the brief's own figures with no gtm.json citation; set as headline/body, never as hero type.

thread.endState: left fully red, right partly filled blue on the final slide

copy.headline: "There's nothing to eat" is a $5,000/year lie.
The average American household spends $3,400/year on food delivery and takeout.
copy.citation: U.S. household delivery spend, USDA / industry data, 2025.

copy.headline: Except there usually is.
copy.body: 60% of wasted food was "forgotten" — pushed to the back of the fridge, buried in the freezer, hidden behind newer purchases.
copy.citation: Food waste behavioral research; ReFED / NRDC "Wasted" report.

copy.headline: So the real equation:
items: You have $40 of food at home.

copy.headline: This happens 2–3x per week.
items: That's $130–195/week in combined waste and delivery.

copy.headline: The fix isn't "cook more" or "meal prep Sunday."
copy.body: The fix is knowing what you have before you open the delivery app.

copy.headline: fond shows you everything in your kitchen and suggests what to cook with it — before you reach for the delivery app.
